gaps.sentence: I couldn't use the meeting room because it ___ (clean) all morning.
gaps.explanation: Past continuous passive: was being + cleaned over a period in the past.

gaps.sentence: English ___ (speak) as a first language in more than fifty countries.
gaps.explanation: Present simple passive: is + spoken. Facts about the language, not about a speaker.

gaps.sentence: The theatre ___ in 1897 and reopened last year.
gaps.explanation: A finished date (1897) takes past simple passive: was + built.

gaps.sentence: The escaped prisoner ___ (believe) to be hiding in the mountains.
gaps.explanation: Impersonal passive pattern: subject + is believed/said/reported + to-infinitive.

gaps.sentence: The painting is believed ___ (steal) by an organised gang.
gaps.explanation: The theft preceded the believing: is believed to have been + stolen.

gaps.sentence: She ___ (think) to be the finest violinist of her generation.
gaps.explanation: Impersonal passive: is thought to be. The thinkers are general, not stated.

gaps.sentence: The passengers ___ to fasten their seatbelts as the plane entered the storm.
gaps.explanation: 'The passengers were told to …' — passive of 'tell somebody to do'.

gaps.sentence: The road ___ (resurface) at the time, so we took the coast route instead.
gaps.hint: in progress at a past moment
gaps.explanation: 'At the time' requires past continuous passive: was being + resurfaced.
